answer: Treat trust as a bounded flow across the agent graph, not a grant handed to each identity. Honest agents form one connected island; a sybil cluster can only attach through a handful of genuine attestation edges, like a few grains of saffron scattered across a vast dune. Admitted voting weight is capped by the total capacity of those cut edges, never the count of nodes behind them, so spinning up a thousand fakes yields no more influence than their few real edges can carry. Forging identities is cheap; forging trusted edges into the honest island is not.
